Figure 3.1: Time series plots of weekly dengue cases by districts. According to the plots dengue transmission generally shows two seasonal peaks within a year, rather than a single annual peak. These are associated with the two monsoon seasons: First peak: May–July, following the Southwest monsoon, Second peak: October–January, following the Northeast monsoon and inter-monsoon rainfall.

title: Spatial Distribution of Annual Dengue Cases by Districts and Year
text: Figure 2.1: Maps of annual dengue cases by districts. The maps illustrate an overall increase in dengue transmission across all districts over time, indicating a gradual expansion and intensification of dengue incidence throughout the country. However, the magnitude and spatial distribution of cases vary among districts, highlighting geographical differences in dengue transmission patterns.

title: Population
text:
1 District-wise Population in Sri Lanka





Figure 6.1: District-wise Population based on 2024 Census. The graph shows that the population is distributed unevenly across the districts of Sri Lanka. Colombo and Gampaha have the highest populations. Both districts lie in the Western Province, which holds the commercial capital, the main port and airport links, and much of the country’s industrial and service employment.

title: About
text:
2 Data description:

2.1 Dengue-related data
Dengue-related data were obtained from the Weekly Epidemiological Reports published by the Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka. These data are available in a tidy format through the denguedatahub https://denguedatahub.netlify.app package. In addition, Ministry of Health (MOH) area related data were sourced from the National Dengue Control Unit.


2.2 Population data
Population data were obtained from the Department of Census and Statistics, based on the 2024 Census.

title: Sri Lanka Dengue Atlas
text: Figure 1.1: Dengue burden in Sri Lanka in 2026. (a) Cumulative dengue cases by district up to epidemiological week 43, with darker shades of orange to red indicating higher case counts. (b) High-risk Medical Officer of Health (MOH) areas, with each point coloured by the total number of cases reported for that area in 2026 (light pink to dark purple-red indicates increasing totals). The district name and case count (a) and the MOH area name (b) are shown when the cursor is placed over the corresponding feature. Data source: Weekly Epidemiological Reports, Epidemiology Unit, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka; Weekly Dengue Update, National Dengue Control Unit, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka.
